NPC IDs:
This is the main page whose information applies to the Desktop, Console, and Mobile versions of Terraria.
For the differences of this information on Old-gen console and 3DS, see Legacy:NPC IDs.
Main article: Data IDs
See also: List of NPCs

This page contains a sortable list of NPC IDs that are used internally in Terraria's game code to reference enemies, critters, and friendly town NPCs (otherwise just referred to as "NPCs"). This information can be useful for research purposes, or in the development of third-party software, like mods and map viewers.

The NPC IDs 76, 146, and 547 are unused. The ID 408 is used for the Flow Invader's minion/projectile: .

Vanity items:
"Vanity" redirects here. For a guide on how to use vanity and customize the character's appearance, see Guide:Vanity.

Vanity items are wearable items that can be equipped in social slots next to the armor and accessories slots in a character's inventory. Wearing them will change a character's appearance, but will not provide any functionality. Vanity items placed in the armor slots will also cover all armor appearances. Many of these vanity items are references to popular culture and other video games.

Interactions with Hair[edit]

The same hairstyle on a character shown in its flat version (left) and its original version (right).

Some head pieces in Terraria show the player's original hair under them, while others hide hair completely, even if that item does not cover the entirety of the player's head. When an item shows player hair, the game will either display the full hairstyle, or a variant of it that flattens the hair so it fits under headgear. This allows items such as the Wizard's Hat to also display the beard of a player. With the exception of the Wizard Hat, armor items generally do not show player hair. Note that, by default, the game hides player hair, so items not listed below hide player hair entirely.

This article is about functional enemy-dropped banners. For decorative banners, see Banners (decorative).

Enemy banners are functional furniture items that can be placed on the underside of blocks, platforms, and Planter Boxes. They are obtained by killing most enemies and a few critters.

Upon reaching a certain kill count (50 by default) of one type of entity in a given world, a banner will automatically appear in the player's Banners Window, located besides the crafting menu. The banner can then be taken out of it, but cannot be placed back inside, similarly to how items cannot be placed inside the crafting window. Additionally, a status message saying "<Player name> has defeated the n-th <enemy name>!" appears, with n being the respective multiple of 50 by default. Not all enemy banners require 50 kills to obtain; see below for a list of exceptions.

When placed, enemy banners provide a Banner buff to any players standing within a rectangular area of 170×125[1] tiles centered on the banner. The buff grants players +50%/+100% damage inflicted with all damage to the corresponding enemy and −25%/−50% damage taken from attacks by the enemy. The banners of Old One's Army enemies will apply a weaker banner buff to the respective enemy, granting the players +10%/+20% damage inflicted and −8.33% / −16.67% damage taken.[a][2]

Multiple banners of the same type will not grant stacked buffs. Multiple different banner types in the vicinity will, however, all take effect and consolidate into a single buff icon. There are a total of 286 obtainable enemy banners: 115 in pre-Hardmode, 171 in Hardmode. Out of these, 118 belong to event enemies (28 in pre-Hardmode and 90 in Hardmode). In addition, there are 6 unobtainable enemy banners.

Banner effect calculation[edit]

Main article: Damage calculations

Notes[edit]

  • Bosses do not have banners, but trophies instead. These do not grant any buffs, however.
  • If an NPC lands the killing blow on an enemy that would have dropped a banner, the last player to hit the enemy receives the banner.
  • The effective range of the buffs from banners is based on the center of the player's view, not where the player is positioned. This can be proven by using Binoculars or a gun equipped with the Sniper Scope or its upgrades.
  • Enemies spawned from Statues count towards the kill count as usual. Because of this, banners for some Hardmode enemies, such as Wraith banners, can be obtained in pre-Hardmode using their respective statues.

Tips[edit]

  • Banners can be suspended under Smoke Blocks and Living Fire Blocks hammered to half blocks or to flat-bottomed slopes. This may be preferred over blocks, platforms, or Planter Boxes, as nothing can collide with Smoke and Living Fire Blocks.
    • However, the War Table Banner immediately breaks when placed.
    • The blocks can be painted with Echo Coating to suspend banners invisibly and with no collision. Likewise, the banners can be painted to provide their buffs invisibly.
    • Living Fire Blocks emit light, while Smoke Blocks do not.

Trivia[edit]

  • Each banner may be placed in a right- or left-facing orientation, but this is decided by which tile column in the world the banner is placed. Placing it one block to the left or right will flip the orientation.
  • The left half of the Nymph Banner depicts the Lost Girl, while the right half is the actual Nymph enemy.
  • The Nymph Banner's internal name is misspelled as NypmhBanner.[6]
  • Diggers share the same banner and kill count with their pre-Hardmode counterparts, the Giant Worms.
  • The Tortured Soul does not have a banner.
  • The Maggot Zombie does not have its own banner; however, the Zombie Banner does offer a buff against it.
  • The Hoplite and Medusa Banners are the only banners that do not show a picture of the enemy. Instead, each resembles dark green banners with golden Greek patterns, with the Hoplite and Medusa Banners having a picture of a helm and snake on them respectively.
  • The Bunny, Bird, Goldfish, and Penguin are the only four critters that have banners of themselves. The four banners still give a buff on attack and defense against the aforementioned critters, even though they cannot actually harm the player.
  • While the player has no banner, the Nurse will muse about a hypothetical "player banner" if spoken to while the player has died at least 25 and less than 100 times (outside of PvP): "The monsters of <world name> have slain you <number of non-PvP deaths> times already? I wonder which one picked up your banner..."
    • This line of dialogue is slightly deprecated as of the 1.4.5.0 update, as enemies no longer drop banners by themselves.
  • The dedicated window for banners located beside the crafting menu was first seen in the March 2024 State of the Game blog.
